nodes.name: Definition 2: Diffeo $f$ with gen hyp Def
nodes.statement:
We say that a diffeomorphism $f:\mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$  satisfies \textit{generalized hyperbolicity} if there exist $C > 0$, $\lambda \in (0, 1)$ and a family of projections $P_x, Q_x: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{B}$ satisfying the following. Denote 
$E^s_x = P_x(\mathbb{B})$, $E^u_x = Q_x(\mathbb{B})$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(GH1)] \textbf{Splitting.} For all $x \in \mathbb{B}$, $P_x + Q_x = Id$, $\|P_x\|, \|Q_x\| \leq C$. In particular $E^s_x \oplus E^u_x = \mathbb{B}$.
    \item[(GH2)] \textbf{Inclusion.} The subspaces $E^s_x$ and $E^u_x$ are invariant under the forward and backward iterations of $Df$, respectively:
    $$
    Df(x)E^s_x \subseteq E^s_{f(x)}, \; D(f^{-1})(x)E^u_x \subseteq E^u_{f^{-1}(x)}, \quad \mbox{ for any $x \in \mathbb{B}$}.
    $$
    \item[(GH3)]  \textbf{Exponential estimates.}  For any $x \in \mathbb{B}$, $n > 0$
    $$
    |Df^n(x)v^s_x| \leq C \lambda^n |v^s_x|, \quad v^s_x \in E^s_x;
    $$
    $$
    |D(f^{-n})(x)v^u_x| \leq C \lambda^n |v^u_x|, \quad v^u_x \in E^u_x.
    $$
\end{itemize}

nodes.name: Theorem 38: Linear shadowing Thm NilsonPeris
nodes.statement: For any invertible continuous linear operator $T$ on any Banach space $X$, if $T$ has the finite Lipschitz shadowing property with constant $L$, then $T$ has the Lipschitz shadowing property with constant $2L$.

nodes.name: Lemma 31: Lem $\{Df(x_k)\}$ has the SBSP
nodes.statement: If $f \in \mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity, then there exists $L>0$ such that, for any exact trajectory $\{x_k\}$ and interval $I$ (finite or infinite), the associated sequence of linear operators $\mathcal{A} = \{A_k = Df(x_k)\}_{k \in I}$ satisfies the strong bounded solution property on $I$ with constant $L$.

nodes.name: Lemma 32: Lem SBSP $\Rightarrow$ BSP under perturbation
nodes.statement:
For any $L > 0$ there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the following holds. Let $I$ be an interval (finite or infinite), and let $\mathcal{A} = \{A_k\}_{k \in I}$ be a sequence satisfying the strong bounded solution property on $I$ with constant $L$. If $\mathcal{B} = \{B_k\}$ is another sequence of uniformly bounded isomorphisms satisfying 
$\|B_k - A_k\| \leq \varepsilon$,
then it satisfies the bounded solution property on $I$ with constant~$2L$.

nodes.name: Lemma 33: Lem finite BSP $\Rightarrow$ BSP on $\mathbb{Z}$
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal A=\{A_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be a sequence of linear isomorphisms such that $\|A_k\|,\|A_k^{-1}\|\leq R$.
 Assume that there exists $L>0$ such that for any finite interval $I = (a, b)$ the sequence $\{A_k\}_{k \in I}$ satisfies the bounded solution property on $I$ with constant $L$. Then the complete sequence $\{A_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ satisfies the bounded solution property on $\mathbb{Z}$ with the constant $2L$.

Lemma 42: Lem finite shadowing
nodes.statement: If $f\in\mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity, then $f$ satisfies the finite Lipschitz shadowing property (FinLipSh).

nodes.name: Lemma 45: Lem BSP $\Rightarrow$ LipSh
nodes.statement: Assume that $f:\mathbb{B}\to\mathbb{B}$ is a $C^1$-diffeomorphism satisfying (4)-(7), and that there exists $d_1, M > 0$ such that, for any $d < d_1$ and any $d$-pseudotrajectory $\{y_k\}$, the sequence ${\mathcal{B}} = \{B_k = Df(y_k)\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ satisfies the bounded solution property with constant $M$. Then $f$ satisfies the Lipschitz shadowing property.

nodes.name: Theorem 11: Thm Lipschitz shadowing
nodes.statement:
Let $f\in\mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ satisfy generalized hyperbolicity. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[
    label=\textup{(M\arabic*)},
    ref=\textup{M\arabic*}
]
    \item 
    $f$ has the Lipschitz shadowing property;
    \item 
    $f$ has the Lipschitz periodic shadowing property;
    \item 
    periodic points are dense in the chain-recurrent set: $\overline{Per(f)}=CR(f)$;
    \item 
    generalized hyperbolicity is robust in the uniform $C^1$
    distance: if $f$ satisfies generalized hyperbolicity with constants
    $C>0$ and $\lambda\in(0,1)$, then, for every
    $\lambda_1\in(\lambda,1)$, there exist $\delta>0$ and $C_1>0$ such
    that every $g\in\mathfrak{D}(\mathbb{B})$ satisfying
    $
    \|g-f\|_{C^1}<\delta
    $
    is generalized hyperbolic with constants $C_1$ and $\lambda_1$.
\end{enumerate}
